overview: This file concerns complaints about Japanese postal service delays, censorship, and confiscation of foreign periodicals, especially those raised by the Reverend Harold J. Schenck of Yokohama. Its principal sequence consists of cross-reference sheets, a May 1936 despatch from American Consul Richard F. Boyce, and an enclosed Japanese postal official’s explanation of censorship policy, including its connection to protection of the national polity and prevention of lèse-majesté. A separate 1933 State Department memorandum records Stanley K. Hornbeck’s preparation of draft correspondence in response to an earlier, unspecified matter involving Mr. Stern and senators from Indiana.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Boyce Despatch No. 202 on mail delays and confiscated magazines
subfiles.about: The sheet directs readers to another file containing Despatch No. 202 concerning Japanese postal delays and Harold J. Schenck’s complaint about confiscated foreign magazines.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Boyce's despatch No. 202 on U.S. mail delays and Schenck's complaint about confiscated foreign magazines.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Yokohama despatch on Japanese censorship of foreign mail
subfiles.about: The sheet refers readers to a despatch explaining Japanese censorship of foreign mail in response to Harold Schenck.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Boyce's May 1936 despatch on Japanese censorship of foreign mail at Yokohama.

subfiles.title: Boyce despatch enclosing a Japanese explanation of postal censorship
subfiles.about: Boyce forwards a Japanese official’s reply to Harold J. Schenck concerning the delivery, censorship, and confiscation of correspondence and printed matter arriving from abroad.
subfiles.summary: Boyce encloses a May 1936 Japanese reply to Schenck's complaint, illustrating Japanese authorities' attitude on censorship of foreign correspondence.

subfiles.title: Japanese postal official’s reply to Harold J. Schenck
subfiles.to: Harold J. Schenck, Union Church, Yokohama
subfiles.about: A Japanese postal official explains and defends the principles governing censorship and confiscation of domestic and foreign periodicals.
subfiles.summary: Japanese postal official declines Schenck's requested public-policy statement, asserting periodicals are judged by content regardless of nationality, linking strict censorship to protecting the national polity and preventing lèse-majesté, while calling page-by-page removal burdensome but possibly acceptable, and praising Schenck's work for friendship.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck memorandum to Hackworth urging prompt action
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Hornbeck submits a memorandum and two tentative draft letters for rapid review because Mr. Stern requested prompt action and the matter could affect relations with Indiana senators.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck tells Hackworth he drafted two letters provisionally, urging prompt action per Stern's request to help the Department with Indiana senators.

interest: Shows Japan's 1930s defense of strict postal censorship protecting the emperor, amid foreign residents' practical mail complaints.
